questions: Should the array indexing for the P_i-th position be considered 1-based (i.e., P_i = 1 inserts at the very beginning) or 0-based?
When inserting the number i at position P_i, does the existing element currently at that position shift right, or is the new element placed after the existing one?
If multiple valid final arrays exist due to ambiguous insertion rules, is there a required tie‑breaking rule for choosing one?
Must the output be printed on a single line with spaces only, or is a trailing space or newline after the last element acceptable?
Are there any constraints on the size of integers that can appear in the output (e.g., should they be printed as 64‑bit integers)?
Is the input guaranteed to have exactly N values for P_i on a single line, or can they be split across multiple lines?
Should the program handle invalid inputs where some P_i > i, and if so, what is the expected behavior (error message, undefined, etc.)?
Are there any time or memory limits that must be adhered to beyond the given N ≤ 5 × 10⁵?

There is an empty array A. For i = 1,2,\ldots,N, perform the following operation in order:
- Insert the number i into A so that it becomes the P_i-th element from the beginning. Not addressed by the given clarifications.
Output the final array A after all operations have been completed.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
P_1 P_2 \ldots P_N
Output
Print A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N in this order, separated by spaces.
Constraints
- 1 \leq N \leq 5\times 10^5
- 1 \leq P_i \leq i
- All input values are integers.
